Different references to a person or title do not create separate lexical senses merely because the record may leave the individual's full name unresolved.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The same graphs also occur as a Chan title and person-name.
EvidenceBody: The Chan Lamp of the Jin River heads a biography “Chan Master Zizhi Zang” (紫芝藏禪師), says that he was born to the Zhang family in Ba County (巴縣張氏子), shaved his head at Great Emei, attended Lingfa Chang for years, received his approval, and later opened the teaching at Zhulin Hall. The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps independently transmits the same Ba-County, Great-Emei, Lingfa-Chang, and Zhulin biography. The Jin River record then marks “lineage heirs of Zizhi Zang” (紫芝藏法嗣). Within that lineage section, Qiongmu Wen's biography says that he heard Zizhi opening the hall, went to meet him, served in the attendant quarters for fifteen years, and was approved (聞紫芝和尚開堂，杖笠往參，充侍寮十五年，遂印可焉). The Recorded Sayings of Zhulangsheng of Qingcheng separately records a direct encounter at Wannian Temple on Emei: Zhulangsheng meets the recorded Chan figure Zizhi (遇紫芝禪師), and the two exchange remarks about Hongchunping, rain pressing on the towers, and leeches along the road. The shared Sichuan and Emei setting makes identification with Zizhi Zang plausible, but that encounter does not supply the name Zang or a lineage statement, so this entry does not declare the identification certain. Zen deployment here is biographical and lineage-bearing: Zizhi opens the hall, approves Qiongmu Wen, has named lineage heirs, and speaks in a recorded encounter.
